newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zaireans flee amid reports of ethnic clashes - UNHCR.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans flee amid reports of ethnic clashes - UNHCR.

text.p: Some 5,000 Zaireans have fled their homes in eastern Zaire after reports of clashes between ethnic Tutsi-led rebels and Rwandan Hutu fighters, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Tuesday.

Spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said that unconfirmed reports of fighting caused panic in an area near Amisi village near the eastern town of Kisangani, with Zairean villagers fleeing towards Lubutu, more than 70 km (44 miles) to the west.

"The security situation in Lubutu is worrying," O'Toole told a briefing, also referring to reports of a Zairean army counter-offensive against the Tutsi-led rebels who took large swathes of eastern Zaire in an uprising in October.
"Reports of clashes have created panic in the area."
In a televised speech on Monday, Zaire's prime minister Kengo wa Dondo ordered a counter-offensive against the rebels.
Preparations have been gathering pace in Kisangani in the heart of Zaire's equatorial rainforest where witnesses report Zairean troops, weapons and as many as 300 foreign mercenaries.
O'Toole said UNHCR had no reports of an exodus among 120,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees in Ting-Tingi, 180 km (120 miles) southeast of Kisangani on the road to the battlefront.
The refugees, joined by former Rwandan government troops and hardline Hutu militiamen who escaped to Zaire after 1994's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis, fled the Tutsi advance to the east.

O'Toole said 20 refugees a day were dying in Tingi-Tingi from disease and malnourishment. UNHCR also confirmed reports of cholera in Tingi-Tingi. The World Health Organisation says cholera killed at least two people there since January 10.
